learn.title: Migration design: Cloud Adoption Framework, assessment and IaaS/PaaS migration
objectives: Apply the Cloud Adoption Framework phases (Strategy, Plan, Ready, Adopt, Govern, Secure, Manage) to a migration programme
Select a migration strategy for each workload: retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, rearchitect, rebuild or replace
Evaluate servers and apps with Azure Migrate: appliance or collector discovery, agentless dependency analysis, readiness, right-sizing and business case
Plan migration waves, cutover methods and rollback using dependency groups and business priorities
Recommend a target and tool for moving servers and apps: Azure VMs, Azure VMware Solution, App Service, Azure Container Apps or AKS
concepts: Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)

Microsoft's guidance for Azure adoption, organised as Strategy, Plan, Ready, Adopt (migrate, modernize, build cloud-native), Govern, Secure and Manage. Its outcome is an Azure landing zone plus operating standards.
Ready phase

The CAF phase that prepares the Azure environment, an Azure landing zone, before workloads move in. Workload migrations should not start until the landing zone (identity, connectivity, DNS, policy) is in place.
Migration strategies (the Rs)
CAF assigns each workload one of: Retire, Retain, Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Rearchitect, Rebuild or Replace, chosen from the business driver for that workload.
Azure Migrate
A free hub for discovering, assessing and migrating servers, databases and web apps. Partner tools in the hub may charge separately.
Azure Migrate appliance
A lightweight appliance deployed on-premises that continuously discovers servers and sends configuration and performance data to Azure Migrate, with nothing installed on the servers being assessed.
Azure Migrate Collector
A snapshot discovery option for air-gapped or restricted networks where an appliance with continuous Azure connectivity isn't feasible.
Agentless dependency analysis

Captures TCP connection data through the appliance with no agents on servers. It works for VMware, Hyper-V, physical and other-cloud servers and is the recommended option; agent-based analysis is classic-only and can't onboard new servers.
Sizing criteria

Performance-based sizing right-sizes from collected CPU, RAM, disk and network data (performance history, percentile utilisation, comfort factor). As-is on-premises sizing matches the current allocation and ignores utilisation.
Azure readiness
Each assessed server is Ready, Conditionally ready, Not ready or Readiness unknown. Servers that fail readiness get no sizing or cost estimate.
Business case
An Azure Migrate report comparing on-premises and Azure TCO, year-over-year cash flow, Azure Arc and ESU savings, with a 'Modernize with PaaS' or 'Migrate to all IaaS' preference.
Migration waves
Groups of workloads moved together, built from dependency groups and priorities: simple and non-production workloads first, critical systems after the team has proven the process.
Azure VMware Solution (AVS)
Dedicated VMware private clouds in Azure. VMware HCX moves VMs without converting them, so teams keep vSphere skills and tools.
comparisons: Rehost moves a workload like-for-like (VM to Azure VM). Replatform moves it to a managed platform such as App Service with only minimal code changes.
Refactor improves the code without changing the architecture. Rearchitect redesigns the architecture, for example into microservices. Rebuild writes a new cloud-native solution from scratch.
Performance-based sizing cuts cost for over-provisioned servers but needs enough collected data. As-is sizing copies the current allocation and doesn't get a performance coverage rating.

Agentless VMware migration reuses the discovery appliance. Agent-based migration uses a replication appliance and is the path for physical servers and VMs from other clouds. Hyper-V migration uses provider agents on the hosts.
App Service vs Container Apps vs AKS
App Service suits web apps that need minimal change. Container Apps runs containers serverlessly without managing Kubernetes. AKS gives full Kubernetes control for teams that need the Kubernetes API.
Azure VMs vs Azure VMware Solution
Azure VMs are the default rehost target and are cheapest when right-sized. AVS fits fast datacenter exits where the team wants to keep VMware tooling and avoid converting VMs.
traps: Don't rehost a workload with known performance or architecture problems; moving it unchanged carries the problems to Azure.
Agent-based dependency analysis isn't available in the new Azure Migrate experience; choose agentless for new projects.
A performance-based assessment run before enough history has been collected gets low performance coverage and unreliable sizes.
Servers imported from CSV and as-is assessments don't get a performance coverage rating.
Retire and Replace aren't the same: retire decommissions a workload, replace moves its users to a SaaS product.
Domain controllers and DHCP servers are usually deployed fresh in Azure rather than migrated.
revision: CAF order: Strategy, Plan, Ready, Adopt; Govern, Secure and Manage run alongside.
Pick each workload's strategy from its business driver, and rehost only workloads that won't need modernising soon.
Deploy the Azure Migrate appliance (or Collector for air-gapped sites) and let it collect data for the whole performance history you'll assess.
Use agentless dependency analysis to build groups of servers that must move together.
Assessment order: readiness, then sizing, then monthly cost.
Build waves: quick wins and non-production first, critical systems later, with tested rollback criteria.
Agentless for VMware, host provider for Hyper-V, replication appliance for physical and other-cloud servers.
App Service for web apps, Container Apps for serverless containers, AKS for full Kubernetes, AVS to keep VMware.

Strategy

Strategy

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: What does the Azure Migrate appliance do when you deploy it in an on-premises datacenter?
opts: It creates the target virtual networks and subnets for migrated servers
It converts on-premises VM disks into Azure managed disks for upload
It installs an agent on each server so that the servers can be replicated
It continuously discovers servers and sends their configuration and performance data to Azure Migrate

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: An Azure VM assessment marks a server as 'Conditionally ready for Azure'. What does this mean?
opts: The server is ready but only after you buy reserved instances
Azure Migrate lacks enough metadata to decide whether the server can run
The server might start in Azure but might not have full Azure support, so you should follow the remediation guidance
The server will not start in Azure until its disks are converted
questions.e: Examples include end-of-support Windows versions and non-endorsed Linux distributions. 'Readiness unknown' is the category used when metadata is missing.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: Why should you run dependency analysis in Azure Migrate before you plan migration waves?
opts: To measure CPU and memory use so that VMs can be right-sized
To estimate the monthly Azure cost of each server
To check whether each operating system is supported in Azure
To find servers that communicate with each other so that they can be grouped and migrated together

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: Most on-premises VMs were allocated far more CPU and memory than they use. You want the Azure VM assessment to recommend the lowest-cost VM sizes that still meet actual demand. Which sizing criterion should you use?
opts: Performance-based sizing
As-is on-premises sizing
Sizing from the VM series list only
As-is sizing with Premium managed disks

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: Which statement best describes Azure VMware Solution as a migration target?
opts: It converts VMware VMs into Azure VMs during replication and removes vSphere
It runs VMware VMs as containers on a shared AKS cluster
It runs dedicated VMware private clouds in Azure, so VMs can move without being converted and teams keep using vSphere tools
It is a free migration tool that moves VMware VMs to App Service

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A company is starting a new Azure Migrate project for VMware and Hyper-V servers. Security policy forbids installing new agents on production servers, and the team must still identify which servers talk to each other. What should you recommend?
opts: Install the Dependency agent on each server and use agent-based analysis
Enable agentless dependency analysis through the Azure Migrate appliance
Enable VM insights on the servers after they have been migrated
Export firewall logs and build the map manually in a spreadsheet
questions.e: Agentless analysis is the recommended option for VMware, Hyper-V, physical and other-cloud servers. Agent-based analysis exists only in the classic view and can't onboard new servers.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: You are assessing servers for a retailer whose demand rises sharply in the holiday season, which is outside the period being profiled. You need Azure VM sizes that leave headroom for that growth. Which assessment setting should you adjust?
opts: Switch the sizing criterion to as-is on-premises sizing
Remove the newer VM series from the assessment
Lower the percentile utilisation to the 50th percentile
Increase the comfort factor
questions.e: The comfort factor is a multiplier applied to CPU, RAM, disk and network data to allow for seasonal usage, short history and future growth.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: An engineer deployed the Azure Migrate appliance yesterday and immediately created a performance-based assessment with one month of performance history. The assessment has a low performance coverage rating. What should you recommend?
opts: Let the appliance collect data for the full month, then recalculate the assessment
Increase the comfort factor to make up for the missing data
Change the target region to one with more VM sizes
Change the percentile utilisation from the 95th to the 99th percentile

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A company needs a rough Azure cost estimate for 400 servers by next week. It already has a CMDB export with each server's cores, memory and disks, and the change board won't approve deploying an appliance in time. What should you recommend?
opts: Install the Azure Monitor Agent on every server to collect inventory
Import the inventory into Azure Migrate with the CSV template and run an assessment
Wait for approval and deploy the Azure Migrate appliance first
Use the Azure pricing calculator to price each server by hand

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A defence contractor wants to discover servers in a restricted network that has no continuous connectivity to Azure, so an always-connected appliance isn't allowed. Which Azure Migrate option should you recommend?
opts: Azure Migrate Collector for a snapshot discovery
Agent-based dependency analysis with Log Analytics
The Azure Migrate appliance with a proxy to the internet
Azure Arc-enabled servers on every machine
questions.e: Azure Migrate Collector takes a point-in-time snapshot and supports air-gapped or restricted networks where an appliance isn't feasible.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: The CFO wants a comparison of on-premises and Azure total cost of ownership, including year-over-year cash flow and savings from Azure Hybrid Benefit, using discovered server data. What should you create in Azure Migrate?
opts: An Azure VM assessment with as-is sizing
A test migration plan
A business case
A dependency analysis export

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A business case must show the savings if web apps and SQL Server instances move to managed services where they fit, while other servers are rehosted. Which migration preference should you select when building the business case?
opts: Azure VMware Solution only
Modernize with PaaS
Migrate to all IaaS
As-is on-premises
questions.e: 'Modernize with PaaS' picks PaaS targets for SQL and web apps where suitable and lift-and-shift for general servers. 'Migrate to all IaaS' sizes everything as Azure VMs.

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A company runs ASP.NET web apps on IIS servers. It wants to stop patching operating systems and gain built-in scaling, but it can only fund minimal code changes. Which migration strategy should you recommend?
opts: Retain the apps on-premises and manage them with Azure Arc
Rehost the IIS servers to Azure VMs
Replatform the apps to Azure App Service
Rearchitect the apps into microservices on AKS

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: An order-processing monolith has one component that needs ten times more capacity than the rest during sales, and teams want to release components independently. Which migration strategy best meets these goals?
opts: Rearchitect
Rehost
Replatform
Retire

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A 20-year-old app is written in an unsupported language, can't be modernised economically, and no SaaS product fits the company's unique process. The business wants new features quickly using PaaS and AI services. Which strategy should you recommend?
opts: Rehost
Refactor
Replace
Rebuild

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A regulator requires a patient records system to stay in the company's own datacenter for at least two more years. The IT team still wants to manage, patch and monitor it from Azure. What should you recommend?
opts: Rehost it to Azure VMs in the nearest region
Replatform it to Azure App Service with private endpoints
Retain the workload on-premises and onboard it to Azure Arc
Retire it and archive its data to Azure Storage

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A team new to Azure is planning its first migration wave. Which workloads should you recommend moving first?
opts: Low-risk internal tools and non-production environments with few dependencies
Every workload that shares the main ERP database
Workloads chosen at random so that each team is represented
The most critical customer-facing system, to show value quickly
questions.e: CAF recommends starting with simple, low-risk and non-production workloads to build skills and refine the process before critical systems.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A company already has an ExpressRoute circuit to Azure and a site-to-site VPN as backup. It will replicate several hundred servers over the network. Which path should you recommend for replication traffic?
opts: Shipping disks with each server image
The public internet
ExpressRoute
The site-to-site VPN

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: You plan to migrate VMs from Hyper-V hosts with Azure Migrate. What does the migration tool rely on for replication?
opts: Azure Site Recovery agents installed in Azure
The VMware vCenter Server that manages the hosts
A Mobility service agent installed inside every VM
Provider agents installed on the Hyper-V hosts
questions.e: Hyper-V migration doesn't need an agent inside each VM. Agent-based migration with the Mobility service is used for physical and other-cloud servers.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A company wants to move 60 VMs from AWS EC2 to Azure VMs using Azure Migrate. How should you recommend migrating them?
opts: Use agentless VMware migration through the discovery appliance
Use the Hyper-V provider on the EC2 hosts
Treat them as physical servers and use agent-based migration with a replication appliance
Export each VM as a VHD and upload it with AzCopy
questions.e: Azure Migrate migrates VMs from other public clouds by treating them as physical servers, using a replication appliance.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: Replication of an app's VMs to Azure has completed. Before the production cutover, the app owner wants to validate the VMs in Azure without affecting the running source servers or ongoing replication. What should you recommend?
opts: Run a test migration into an isolated, non-production virtual network
Run the final migration and roll back if tests fail
Restore the latest on-premises backup into Azure and test that copy
Stop replication and start the VMs in the production virtual network
questions.e: A test migration creates VMs in a network you choose while replication continues, so production is unaffected.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A company has hundreds of ASP.NET web apps on IIS servers spread across a VMware environment. It wants to discover, assess and migrate them to Azure App Service in bulk with the least manual effort. What should you recommend?
opts: App Service Migration Assistant run on each IIS server in turn
Rebuild each app in a new repository and deploy with GitHub Actions
Azure Migrate at-scale discovery, assessment and migration of ASP.NET web apps
Rehost every IIS server to Azure VMs with agentless migration

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A small charity has one ASP.NET web app on a single on-premises IIS server and wants a free, simple tool to move it to Azure App Service. What should you recommend?
opts: Agent-based migration with a replication appliance
App Service Migration Assistant
Azure VMware Solution with VMware HCX
Azure Database Migration Service

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A .NET Framework web app depends on registry settings and Windows configuration scripts that standard App Service doesn't allow. The company wants a PaaS target with the least refactoring. What should you recommend?
opts: A standard App Service plan on Linux
Azure Static Web Apps
Managed Instance on Azure App Service
Azure Functions on the Flex Consumption plan
questions.e: Managed Instance on App Service supports configuration scripts, registry adapters, storage mounts and private networking for apps that rely on Windows features.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A team has containerised several stateless microservices. It wants event-driven autoscaling, including scale to zero, without managing Kubernetes clusters or upgrades. Which target should you recommend?
opts: Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure Container Apps
Azure VMware Solution
Azure VMs in a scale set
questions.e: Container Apps is built on Kubernetes but hides cluster management and supports KEDA-based scaling, including scale to zero.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A platform team is migrating containerised apps that rely on custom Kubernetes operators, direct access to the Kubernetes API and specific node pool settings. Which target should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Instances
Azure App Service for Containers
Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure Container Apps

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A company must reproduce exactly the CPU and memory each server has today because a vendor's support contract requires matching specifications. Which sizing criterion should the Azure VM assessment use?
opts: As-is on-premises
Performance-based with a one-day history
Performance-based with a high comfort factor
Performance-based with the 95th percentile

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A trading app has short, important CPU bursts that the default rightsizing ignores. You want performance-based sizing to cover peak usage, including outliers. What should you set?
opts: Percentile utilisation to the 50th percentile
Sizing criterion to as-is on-premises
Percentile utilisation to the 99th percentile
Performance history to one day
questions.e: The 95th percentile ignores outliers. Choose the 99th percentile when you want sizing based on peak usage.

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: Dependency analysis shows that an app server makes thousands of low-latency calls per minute to a database server. How should you plan their migration?
opts: Migrate both servers in the same wave
Migrate the database first and the app server a few months later
Migrate the app server first and keep the database on-premises
Migrate them in separate waves to reduce the size of each wave

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: According to the Cloud Adoption Framework, when should you define the criteria that trigger a rollback for a workload migration?
opts: Only for workloads that use near-zero downtime migration
After the first failed health check in production
During the post-migration optimisation step
Before the migration starts, agreed with business and workload owners

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Azure Migrate dependency analysis in the current experience. 1: Agentless analysis needs no agents on the analysed servers. 2: Agentless analysis supports VMware VMs, Hyper-V VMs and physical servers. 3: New servers can be onboarded to agent-based analysis. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
questions.e: Agent-based analysis is only in the classic view, which is being deprecated, and new servers can't be onboarded to it.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Azure VM assessments. 1: Readiness is calculated before sizing and cost. 2: A server marked Not ready still gets a monthly cost estimate. 3: If several VM sizes meet the requirements, the lowest-cost size is recommended. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statement 1 only
questions.e: Servers move to sizing and cost only after passing readiness, and the cheapest eligible size is chosen.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: After migration, Azure VMs sized by a performance-based assessment are overloaded every month-end close. The assessment used one day of performance history, captured mid-month. What should you have recommended?
opts: Use as-is sizing so that every VM is smaller
Use a performance history that covers the month-end close, such as one month
Exclude the newest VM series from the assessment
Lower the comfort factor to reduce over-sizing

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A workload must stay in the company's datacenter because of data residency law, but the company wants Azure management. Which approach should you NOT recommend?
opts: Rehost the workload to Azure VMs in a nearby region
Retain it and onboard the servers to Azure Arc
Retain it and revisit the decision in a later wave if the law changes
Retain it and refresh the hardware with Azure Local

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: A company has Windows Server licences with active Software Assurance. Most servers run 24x7 with steady load. You need the Azure VM assessment to show the lowest realistic compute cost. Which assessment settings should you use?
opts: Disable Azure Hybrid Benefit and set VM uptime to 8 hours a day
Select Ultra Disk storage and the pay-as-you-go offer only
Use as-is sizing and leave the savings option as None
Enable Azure Hybrid Benefit and select a reserved instance or savings plan option

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: An app has three ASP.NET front ends on IIS, two Windows servers running a third-party service that needs full OS access. The company wants to reduce OS patching where possible, keep effort low and finish within one quarter. What should you recommend for the front ends and the service servers?
opts: Rearchitect the front ends and service into microservices on AKS
Replatform the front ends to App Service and rehost the service servers to Azure VMs
Rehost all five servers to Azure VMs and modernise nothing
Move all five servers to Azure VMware Solution and modernise later

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: Dependency maps show that three apps share one SQL Server instance, and it's unclear how latency-sensitive two of the connections are. The waves are already large. How should you plan the waves?
opts: Move the database first and test the apps over the VPN for a month
Split the apps across waves to keep each wave small
Group the three apps and the database in the same wave
Move each app in its own wave and leave the database on-premises
questions.e: When dependency criticality is uncertain, CAF recommends grouping components together; they can be separated later if it proves safe.

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: Agentless dependency analysis is enabled for a group of VMware VMs, but no dependency data appears for some servers even after a day. Configuration and performance data for them is visible. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The appliance has no valid guest credentials for those servers, so software inventory and dependency collection can't run
The Dependency agent hasn't been installed on those servers
Agentless analysis is supported only for Hyper-V VMs
The assessment uses as-is sizing instead of performance-based sizing

questions.on: Recommend a solution for migrating workloads to IaaS and PaaS
questions.q: A company is migrating 800 VMware VMs and 40 physical servers to Azure VMs. It wants to avoid installing agents wherever possible and reuse the discovery appliance already deployed. What should you recommend?
opts: Agent-based migration for all servers with one replication appliance
Azure VMware Solution for the VMs and App Service for the physical servers
Agentless migration for all servers through the discovery appliance
Agentless migration for the VMware VMs and agent-based migration with a replication appliance for the physical servers

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: Map tasks to Cloud Adoption Framework phases. 1: Defining policies and a governance team before workloads are deployed belongs to Govern. 2: Building the operational baseline for monitoring and optimising workloads over time belongs to Manage. 3: Choosing the migration strategy for each workload belongs to Ready. Which statements are correct?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 1 and 3 only
questions.e: Strategy selection is part of Plan. Ready is about building the landing zone.

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: A team plans to rehost an app now, but the product owner says it will be split into microservices next year to support a new product line. Which change to the plan should you recommend?
opts: Rehost it now to Azure VMware Solution to keep options open
Retire the app and rebuild it after the datacenter exit
Modernise the app during migration instead of rehosting it and reworking it later
Rehost it now and buy a three-year reservation for its VMs
questions.e: CAF advises rehosting only workloads that won't need modernising within about two years, to avoid doing the work twice.

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: An app on-premises suffers frequent outages caused by its single-server design. The migration plan says to rehost it as-is so that 'Azure will fix the reliability'. Why is this plan flawed?
opts: Rehosted VMs can't be added to availability zones later
Rehosting keeps the same architecture, so the reliability problems move to Azure unchanged
Azure Migrate can't rehost servers that have had outages
Rehosting is only supported for Linux servers

questions.on: Evaluate a migration solution that leverages the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
questions.q: For an enterprise migrating existing workloads, which activity is NOT part of the Cloud Adoption Framework Plan phase?
opts: Estimating the cost of the workloads in Azure
Selecting a migration strategy for each workload
Deploying the Azure landing zone
Discovering and inventorying the existing workloads

questions.on: Evaluate on-premises servers, data, and applications for migration
questions.q: An engineer enabled agentless dependency analysis 30 minutes ago and reports that the dependency map in the Azure portal is still empty, though discovery is healthy. What should you tell them?
opts: Dependency analysis requires an Azure VMware Solution private cloud
The appliance collects connection data locally and sends it to Azure Migrate every six hours, so wait for the next upload
The map stays empty until the Dependency agent is installed
Dependency data appears only after a performance-based assessment is created

questions.e: CAF calls high-value, low-effort workloads quick wins. High-value, high-effort ones are strategic investments that need careful planning.
